# `Q-21-5` — Inline Reference Not Available To Typst

> A citation refers to an entry defined only in the front-matter
> `references:` list, which Typst's own bibliography does not read.

## What this means

By default, Typst output formats citations with Typst's own
bibliography, not with citeproc. Each citation reaches Typst as
`@key`, and Typst looks the key up in the files listed in
`bibliography:`. Entries written directly in the document's front
matter under `references:` are not in any of those files, so Typst
cannot find them.

Without this check, `typst compile` would stop with
`label <key> does not exist in the document`. Quarto reports the
problem before Typst runs, and points at the citation.

When the render produces Typst source instead of a PDF (an `output-ext`
other than `pdf`), Typst does not run, so this is a warning: the source
is still written, but compiling it will fail the same way.

## Why this happens

- The document lists its references in front matter instead of a
  bibliography file:

  ``` yaml
  ---
  format: typst
  references:
    - id: smith2020
      type: webpage
      title: A page
  ---

  See [@smith2020].
  ```

- The document has a `bibliography:` file, but the cited entry is only
  in `references:`.
- `citation-location: margin` is set. Margin citations also use
  Typst's own bibliography, in documents and in books.

## How to fix

Either of these works:

- Set `citeproc: true`. Citeproc then formats the citations and the
  bibliography, and it reads `references:` as well as `bibliography:`.
  The output uses a CSL style instead of a Typst bibliography style.
- Move the entry into a bibliography file, BibLaTeX `.bib` or Hayagriva
  `.yml`, and list that file under `bibliography:`.
